A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neural Entropy and provide readable text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–E. The corresponding material can be matched reliably; v3 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian-mixture, MNIST, and CIFAR-10 experiments in Section 6 and the appendices, including entropy measurements and generated images.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their outcomes in Section 6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The entropy-matching objective, neural-entropy estimator, architectures, and sampling procedures are retained. The time-argument correction in Eq. (13a) aligns it with the reverse process already documented in Appendix B, rather than establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture tasks, unconditional MNIST generation, and conditional CIFAR-10 generation. No evaluated dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The VP, VPx, and Straight Line comparisons remain unchanged, as does the entropy-matching versus score-matching comparison in Figure 9. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain the same sample counts, dimensionalities, training epochs, diffusion schedules, truncation rules, and KL/cross-entropy evaluation procedures. The new theoretical restriction does not change the reported experimental settings.

E4.justification: The analyses of diffusion processes, dimensionality, training-set size, score-matching entropy, and generated-image quality are retained. No ablation, sensitivity analysis, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both Appendix E versions specify four random seeds, except for Figure 9, varying initialization and training order, with bands showing one standard deviation. The added checklist repeats this existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: The corresponding plots and image samples are unchanged. Both versions report the same image-model entropy scaling and VP versus VPx/SL findings, with no added, removed, or revised empirical result entries.

T1.justification: v3 materially narrows the central entropy–KL identity in Eq. (15) to processes with b+/σ² constant in time. It removes the unconditional zero time derivative from Eq. (14) and explicitly invokes the new restriction in the H-theorem proof, formerly B.2 and now B.3. This changes the stated validity scope of a central theoretical result. Eq. (13a) also corrects σ(t)² to σ(T−t)².

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: neural entropy as a process-dependent information measure and empirical evidence of efficient image-distribution compression with approximately logarithmic entropy growth.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly states the constant-in-time b+/σ² restriction, clarifying the applicability boundary of Eq. (15). Interpretations of the experimental findings and the limitations discussed in Section 7 otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains the same implementation details, hardware, runtimes, and estimation procedures. The checklist repeats existing disclosures and links to the same code repository already identified in v2; it supplies no substantive new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 adds Sharp and Matschinsky’s translation of Boltzmann, Kong et al.’s Information-theoretic diffusion, and Franzese et al.’s MINDE. The related-work paragraph briefly expands its information-theoretic context without substantially repositioning the contribution.

P1.justification: v3 adds a coin-toss analogy and a NeurIPS checklist, numbers the existing notation subsection as B.1, corrects cross-references, and updates affiliation and publication text. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: All 18 figures retain their graphical content. Figure 6 moves within Appendix B, text and references reflow, bibliography back-references are added, and conference/checklist formatting extends the document. There is no substantial redesign of the scientific displays.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the overgeneral presentation of Eq. (15) by stating the time-invariance condition and using it in the appendix proof. The narrower theoretical scope is more defensible, while the retained experiments already use compatible processes. Corrected time arguments and cross-references, plus relevant citations, provide additional modest benefits; the empirical evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
